chunks: 1994 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said:
I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: My wife had made it binding upon herself to fast for two months, then she gave birth to her child and pregnancy came upon her, so she was unable to fast.
He said: Let her give in charity, in place of each day, one mudd to a poor person.

key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ: two months; the duration of the fast she had undertaken
key_terms.صَوْمَ: fasting; the vowed devotional fast in question
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a mudd; a measured amount given as charity
key_terms.مِسْكِينٍ: a poor person; the recipient of the charity
key_terms.ٱلصَّوْمِ: the fast; the act she was unable to perform
key_terms.ٱلْحَبَلُ: pregnancy; the condition that prevented her from fasting

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she vowed to fast but became unable due to childbirth and pregnancy?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a woman who had obligated herself to fast for two months but became unable to do so due to childbirth and a subsequent pregnancy. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructs that she should give charity equal to one mudd of food to a poor person for each missed day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1994 - It was narrated by Ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Ja'far:
"I said to Abu al-Hasan (as): 'My wife took upon herself to fast for two months, but she gave birth and then became pregnant again, so she was unable to fast.'
Imam (as) said: 'She should give in charity for each day a mudd (measure) to a poor person.'"
